changes.remove: Quite a lot more, and the finish is the reason. In honest all-original condition a Competition guitar from 1969 to 1973 runs roughly $4,000 to $6,000, against roughly $1,600 to $2,200 for a CBS-era standard colour and $2,200 to $4,000 for a pre-CBS 1964 or 1965. Competition Orange is the rarest of the three colours and can run above that, and Competition Blue carries extra weight from the Nirvana association. Because the buyer is paying for the finish, a refinished Competition guitar loses most of the premium, which is a bigger gap than a refinish costs on a plain Mustang.
changes.replaceWith: A Competition Mustang has a factory racing stripe and the corresponding Competition finish. I compare the stripe, pickguard, headstock finish and dated parts to identify the configuration. A later stripe or a refinish doesn't establish an original Competition model.
